notes:
BUILD 64
- Engine, the way Rust does it. Five parts: crankshaft, pistons, spark plugs, air filter, gaskets, each in three qualities: Low Quality, regular, and High Quality. All five have to be fitted and not worn out for the engine to run. Parts wear as you drive: low quality lasts about fifteen minutes of driving, regular forty, high ninety. Better parts give the engine more: a full high quality set is 40% stronger and 25% faster at the top end.
- Only low quality parts are found (barrels, road cars) or sold (Resource Exchange, 30 scrap). All three qualities can be crafted: low at a level 1 bench from the start, regular at level 2 and high at level 3 once researched. The old carburetor and valves no longer fit anything.
- A car has three places to walk up to. The hood at the front opens the engine: fuel and the five parts. The bed at the back opens the cargo. The doors in the middle are where you get in. Whatever is in the bed shows as boxes stacked in it.
- Water: driving through deep water (over the sills) floods the engine a little at a time, shown as TAKING IN WATER. If it fills, the engine dies and the air filter is ruined: fit a new one. A quick ford is fine.
- Heavier, calmer car: more weight on the springs, firmer damping, and the springs can no longer throw it into the air off a bank.
- The mouse looks around freely while you drive a car or a boat.
- Hitting things: the car is damaged by how hard it hits (trees, rocks, walls), and it damages what it hits by its speed: animals, scientists, barrels, turrets. Cars also take damage from gunfire, and one shot to nothing blows up even if nobody is in it.
- Only vehicles that are yours are marked on the map and compass: ones you bought, and cars you have sat in. Cars have their own orange icon and a C on the compass; dinghies a hull and a B. In your current save the road cars drop off the map until you get into each one again.
- Cars are solid to walk into along their whole length and width.
- Icons are drawn a little smaller on their sheet to make room for the new items.
